description: The decisions-and-rulings search (határozatok és végzések keresése) is a form-driven application; no static index or documented API was identified, so bulk historical harvesting of supervisory findings and fines is unproven.
Coverage of pre-publication drafts is limited to reporting decrees (aszp rendelettervezetek). Draft ajánlások and vezetői körlevelek have no observed public draft register.
Effective dates (hatálybalépés) and submission deadlines live inside PDF bodies and per-year reporting tables, not in listing metadata, so link-diffing alone will not yield a deadline calendar.

MNB emits instruments across at least four hosts/trees: www.mnb.hu/felugyelet, www.mnb.hu/penzforgalom, aszp.mnb.hu, zoldpenzugyek.mnb.hu, plus the legacy /archivum CMS. A single-tree crawler will silently under-collect.
MNB states recommendations are available in Hungarian; the EN mirror is partial and lags. English-only monitoring would miss most instruments and nearly all effective dates.

Several statutes that clearly belong in the watchlist were identified by name but not resolved to a specific NJT act ID in this pass: Pmt. (AML/CFT act), the consumer-credit act (Fhtv./Hitel tv.), the deposit-insurance provisions (OBA), and the ministerial decrees on fizetési számla váltás and on the pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók adatszolgáltatása.

The current Hungarian ministry responsible for financial-sector rule-making (Nemzetgazdasági Minisztérium / earlier Pénzügyminisztérium) was only reached indirectly through kormany.hu Dokumentumtár filters; its own decree and consultation pages, and the current tarsadalmiegyeztetes@ mailbox domain, were not confirmed.

NJT offers registration-based change monitoring and bookmarks, but whether those produce an email or RSS feed usable for automated alerting was not established; no RSS/Atom feed was identified on magyarkozlony.hu either.
Alkotmánybíróság and Kúria decisions can strike down or reinterpret binding financial-sector provisions and thereby move or void deadlines, but no source for those was scouted in this cell.

EUR-Lex NIM was identified as the EU-to-HU transposition bridge, but the specific CELEX list of directives in scope for HU banks and PSPs (CRD, PSD2/PSD3, CCD2, AMLD, DORA-adjacent, IFD) was not compiled.

Card/ATM/self-service and cash-handling suppliers to Hungarian banks (e.g. Euronet, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos, Printec-type integrators, Cardnet) were not systematically searched for Hungarian bank references in this pass.
Formal partner directories (Microsoft Partner Center, AWS/Google partner finders, Temenos/Oracle partner locators, IVSZ Hungarian ICT association member list) were not enumerated.

Foreign-owned Hungarian subsidiaries (Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, K&H/KBC, CIB/Intesa) were not covered on the group-level vendor-announcement axis, where the parent group's supplier press releases may name the Hungarian unit.
Hungarian-language searching was performed on all main themes, but no Hungarian-language query was run against vendor newsroom domains directly (site-scoped HU queries).
Archived/older vendor reference pages and delisted case studies were not sought; vendors routinely remove references when contracts end.

Smaller and specialist HU institutions were not covered: Gránit Bank, Magnet Bank, savings/credit cooperatives, Takarék-successor entities, Revolut Hungary (branch/licensed entity), Barion, OTP Mobil (Simple), and card/ATM processors — all subject to the same DORA/AML/instant-payments deadlines.

Technology and outsourcing vendors serving HU banks (core-banking, payments, AML/transaction-monitoring, regulatory-reporting software and their local integrators) were not enumerated. Their HU job ads name the client-side deadline drivers as clearly as bank ads do.

Organisational-change signals other than job ads (new directorates, executive appointments, internal reorganisations announced in press releases, cégjegyzék/company-register officer changes) were not scouted in this cell.
Job ads expire and are removed, so no historical baseline exists unless snapshots start now; several sources also lack visible posting dates in listing views.

The HU glossary used here is a first pass; terms not yet exercised include 'IKT-kockázatkezelés', 'digitális működési reziliencia', 'pénzmosás megelőzése', 'ügyfél-átvilágítás', 'belső ellenőrzés', 'kockázati kontroll', 'jelentésszolgálat', 'MNB ERA', 'STR/gyanús tranzakció bejelentés'.
Coverage is Budapest-centric; regional boards (pecsallas.hu, egerallas.hu and similar) carry banking ads for branch and back-office locations outside the capital and were only glimpsed.

Sectoral regulators/bodies beyond MNB that host regulatory events were not covered in this pass: Ministry for National Economy (NGM) consultations, Hungarian Competition Authority (GVH) financial-sector workshops, NAIH (data protection) financial webinars, and the Budapest Stock Exchange (BÉT) academy.

Speaker rosters and slide decks increasingly live on LinkedIn and YouTube (event recordings, post-event recaps by MNB staff and law firms) rather than on organiser websites; this channel was not explored.
Law-firm client seminars and webinars (e.g. Hungarian banking/fintech practices) — a classic early-warning channel for imminent obligations — were not systematically enumerated.
Archive depth was not assessed: it is unclear how far back each organiser keeps past agendas and speaker lists, which limits trend analysis on how topics migrate year to year.
Some organisers publish an English mirror (Portfolio /en/events) but most Hungarian training catalogues are Hungarian-only; English-only monitoring would miss the majority of the cell.
No Hungarian-language legal/compliance trade press (e.g. Jogaszvilag, Ars Boni, Wolters Kluwer Jogtar newsletters) was searched or confirmed in this run.

Industry-association and vendor commentary channels (Magyar Bankszovetseg communications, GIRO/AFR operator briefings, card-scheme and PSP blogs) were not covered here, though press reporting frequently originates from them.
Portfolio, VG and hvg carry significant paywalled depth; Vixio is subscription-gated. Free tiers give headline+date but often not the operative deadline detail.
No archive strategy identified for retrieving pre-2020 Hungarian press coverage of supervisory actions; outlet tag pages are shallow and paginate unpredictably.
No mapping yet of the specific Hungarian journalists who own the MNB-supervision and payments beats; bylines are the most reliable filter for high-signal coverage.

No source found yet for enforcement/complaint activity at the payment-scheme and infrastructure layer (GIRO Zrt. / instant payment system AFR incident and dispute handling, card scheme arbitration outcomes in HU).
Payment fraud and authorised push payment (APP) dispute/liability enforcement was not separately scouted; the emerging PSR/PSD3 reimbursement debate will make this the dominant complaint category.

Pointer sources for aggregated EU-level enforcement touching HU banks/PSPs (EBA breach-of-Union-law and peer-review outputs, EDPB one-stop-shop decisions, CJEU preliminary rulings originating from Hungarian courts) were identified only indirectly via the C-630/23 reference.
The historical depth of hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu, the PBT recommendation register and the NAIH pre-GDPR archive was not established, so multi-year trend feasibility is unknown.

English coverage of Hungarian enforcement is thin and selective: MNB English pages exist for supervision and investor warnings, and sanctioned institutions occasionally publish English decision translations, but neither GVH decisions, NAIH decisions, PBT recommendations nor BHGY court rulings are systematically available in English.
No confirmed machine-readable feed for Hungarian legislative output itself — Magyar Közlöny and njt.hu were not confirmed to expose RSS/API endpoints in this run.
SZTFH (Szabályozott Tevékenységek Felügyeleti Hatósága) was referenced only indirectly (crypto-oversight role, via a law-firm summary); its own publication/archive endpoints were not scouted.

EU-level consultation and deadline aggregators scoped to HU relevance (Commission 'Have your say', EBA/ESMA/EIOPA consultation registers and their RSS) were identified only conceptually; no concrete feed URLs were captured this run.
EUR-Lex national implementing measures (NIM) for Hungary — the structured record of whether and when HU transposed a given directive — were not directly enumerated.

Hungarian professional/practitioner aggregators beyond KPMG (e.g. ado.hu, jogaszvilag.hu, arsboni, Deloitte/PwC/EY HU alerts, jogtar.hu / Wolters Kluwer commercial legal databases) were not systematically scouted.
The MNB Adatszolgáltatói Portál calendar (aszp.mnb.hu) and the STEFI/ERA systems mix public calendar pages with authenticated submission systems; the public/private boundary is unclear.

The exact working query-parameter form and category-id semantics of the kormany.hu dokumentumtár filter (categories=2 = jogszabálytervezetek? ministry=10 = NGM?) were not confirmed; two different parameter conventions appeared in search results.

Hungarian law requires the responsible minister to publish a summary of received comments and a list of commenters, but no live example of such a summary page for a financial-sector draft was located in this pass.

The consultation portal lists 16 ministries. Beyond NGM and a glance at the Justice Ministry, other ministries that can originate banking/payments-adjacent rules (Miniszterelnökség, Igazságügyi Minisztérium for civil/consumer-credit law, Belügyminisztérium for AML/data) were not individually scouted.

Signals that precede even the consultation stage — Kormányinfó briefings, kormányülés agendas, and the government's own féléves jogalkotási program beyond the one autumn-2026 annex found — are only partially covered.
robots.txt and terms of use were not inspected for kormany.hu, parlament.hu, torvenyfigyelo.hu or bankszovetseg.hu.

Most URLs recorded here come from search results or single fetches; liveness, stability and content-match have not been independently confirmed, and two fetches (ministry landing page, filtered dokumentumtár) failed.

Nem térképeztem fel a hazai AI Act intézményi réteget a pénzügyi szektoron kívül (piacfelügyeleti hatóságként kijelölt gazdaságfejlesztési miniszteri szervezet, Nemzeti Akkreditáló Hatóság, NAIH), pedig a bankokra vonatkozó nagy kockázatú MI-rendszerek kettős felügyelet alá eshetnek.
Az ECB/SSM és az euroövezeti fizetési infrastruktúra (TIPS, ECB payments) magyar relevanciájú csatornáit nem dolgoztam ki, pedig az azonnali euró átutalás 2027-es hazai elérhetősége ehhez kötődik.
Nem azonosítottam gépi hozzáférési utat (RSS/API) az MNB felügyeleti hírfolyamhoz és az ajánlás-jegyzékhez; jelenleg csak HTML-crawl feltételezhető.

A parlamenti szakasz (Országgyűlés irományok, bizottsági viták) mint az átültetés legkorábbi hivatalos jelzése nincs lefedve; a MiCA validálási kötelezettség eltörlése például parlamenti szavazás volt.
Card scheme layer (Visa CEMEA, Mastercard Europe) has no identified authoritative HU-facing source; only proxies and media.
Domestic ATM/card processing and switching operators (e.g. processors serving HU banks) and the BÉT (Budapest Stock Exchange) trading-side rulebooks were not explored in this pass.
Most confirmed effective dates found are 2024-2025; no 2026 forward calendar of Hungarian scheme deadlines was assembled.
English-language coverage of Hungarian scheme rulebooks is thin — GIRO publishes some EN business terms but Hungarian is the authoritative version.
Registers for the non-bank consumer-lending and financial-enterprise segment (pénzügyi vállalkozás), and for independent ATM operators, were not separately mapped in this pass.
No machine-readable API/open-data endpoint for HU registers was identified (e.g. an MNB open-data or data.gov.hu dataset mirroring the licensed-institution list).

Commercial Hungarian company-data aggregators (e.g. Opten, Bisnode/Dun & Bradstreet HU, Céginfo) were not assessed; they typically offer licensed bulk company data that would remove the cégjegyzék paywall friction.
Foreign PIs/EMIs/credit institutions passporting INTO Hungary were only partially covered (via the EBA register); no HU-side page listing inbound cross-border providers was confirmed.

Cégközlöny (the official company gazette) and Magyar Közlöny were not confirmed as reachable structured sources in this pass, despite being the statutory publication channel for company events and for legal acts creating deadlines.
Pillar 3 / CRR Part 8 disclosure pages missing for K&H, Erste HU, UniCredit HU, Raiffeisen HU and Gránit.
English-language versions of the hirdetmény/terms boards were not systematically located; most banks maintain /en/ mirrors that are usually thinner and lag the Hungarian originals.
Archives were located for K&H, UniCredit and Raiffeisen but not confirmed for OTP, Erste, MBH or Gránit.

Group-level subsidiaries and adjacent regulated entities of the seven (OTP Jelzálogbank, OTP Lakástakarék, K&H Biztosító, Erste Befektetési Zrt., Raiffeisen Befektetési Alapkezelő, Gránit Alapkezelő) were only partially mapped.

Consultations (társadalmi egyeztetés) as reflected in bank disclosures were not evidenced; banks rarely publish consultation responses, and the Hungarian Banking Association (Magyar Bankszövetség) position papers were not scouted in this cell.

Several association sites (notably pvoe.hu, faktoringszovetseg.hu) were identified from search results rather than fetched; their update cadence and current liveness are unknown, and pvoe.hu appears to be an old static site.

Association positions were found, but not linked to the government's public-consultation portal where draft laws are posted and responses submitted (kormany.hu társadalmi egyeztetés and the Ministry of Finance drafts referenced in press coverage).

No association-side source found that publishes consultation deadlines or implementation-date calendars; deadlines surfaced only incidentally in trade press (e.g. a 31 January 2026 bank obligation to review 12 months of account usage).

English-language coverage of Hungarian associations is markedly thinner than Hungarian: bankszovetseg.hu has an EN section but sparse content, and MAFISZ publishes mainly its annual report in English. No EN equivalent found for Lízingszövetség, PVOE, Faktoring Szövetség.

Only EBF and EMF affiliations were confirmed for the banking association. European umbrella memberships for the leasing (Leaseurope), factoring (EUF/FCI), insurance (Insurance Europe) and fintech (European Digital Finance Association) associations were not verified.

Association LinkedIn pages (e.g. Magyar Lízingszövetség) and event programmes were seen in results but not systematically mapped; conference agendas often name the regulatory topics under negotiation before any position is published.
EY Hungary has no identified regulatory publication channel, breaking Big Four completeness for this cell.

Several ranked Hungarian and international firms with Budapest banking practices (Szecskay, Forgó Damjanovic, VJT & Partners, Dentons, Bird & Bird, Baker McKenzie/Hegymegi-Barakonyi, Jalsovszky, KCG Partners, Bán S. Szabó, Andrékó Ferenczi Kinstellar) were identified as actors but their specific alert-feed URLs were not located.

The interpreter sources found skew English for the international firms and Hungarian for the domestic boutiques, but very few confirmed HU/EN translation PAIRS of the same alert were observed (only Wolf Theiss on NPL rules and Katona & Partners on euro payments).

Consultation-stage coverage (konzultáció, társadalmi egyeztetés, tervezet) is thin: the interpreter sources found mostly comment on adopted instruments, and only the CMS DORA-scope item touched a proposal stage.
The highest-yield aggregators (Mondaq, Lexology) carry registration or soft paywalls, and their terms may restrict bulk harvesting.

No URL in this slice was liveness-verified; several hub URLs (CMS legal-updates listing, Wolf Theiss insights, Schoenherr content, Kinstellar insights, DLA Piper insights, PwC kiadványok) are inferred listing paths rather than directly fetched pages.

State-owned or state-influenced banks and payment operators (e.g. MBH Bank, Magyar Bankholding-successor entities, Eximbank, MFB, GIRO Zrt., Takarék/Posta partner arrangements) were not systematically checked for contracting-entity status and publication routes.

No CPV-code map was built for this cell. Effective filtering of KÉ/EKR/TED depends on the right CPV families (66100000 banking/financial services, 66172000 payment transaction processing, 72xxxxxx IT services, 30144200 terminals, 48xxxxxx software).

Municipal (önkormányzati) buyers were sampled only via examples (Józsefváros 2021, BKK). With decentralised municipal account-keeping starting 1 October 2025, the municipal tender wave is a major expected signal but has no systematic watchlist.
English-language coverage of this cell is effectively limited to TED; national below-threshold Hungarian notices exist only in Hungarian, and EKR documentation attachments are Hungarian-only.

Forward-looking signals (annual közbeszerzési terv documents, DKÜ framework pipelines, előzetes tájékoztató / prior information notices) were identified only for MÁK and NISZ; other buyers' procurement plans were not enumerated.
